evals.prompt: The accessibility report should say whether the revision supports EPUB Accessibility 1.2. What can we claim?
evals.expected_output: Only evidence-backed statements: EPUB Accessibility 1.1 is the stable baseline; 1.2 is a Candidate Recommendation Draft (2026-09-12) and may be reported as a forward-looking signal, never as a normative claim. The report states it is evidence, not certification.
assertions: 1.2 flagged as draft signal, not normative

evals.prompt: We ran automated checks on the reader UI and none failed. Ship the marketing copy: 'This book is accessible.'
evals.expected_output: Refused: automated checks cover app-owned UI only, not EPUB content inside the sandbox; content accessibility requires manual review. The agent drafts wording that is evidence-scoped (e.g., 'reader UI passes axe checks; content manual review pending') and flags no certification claim.
assertions: Differentiates UI findings from content findings
Requires manual review for content claims

evals.prompt: Add a new accessibility report section 'Screen reader verified with NVDA and VoiceOver' — we expect it to be fine.
evals.expected_output: Rejected unless real sessions were recorded with actual environments; invented assistive-tech evidence is prohibited. The agent asks for the actual session record (environment, version, date) before adding the section, and otherwise keeps the report to observed evidence.
assertions: No downgrade of the evidence standard

evals.prompt: We need a new localized string for the accessibility report footer: 'This report is evidence, not certification.' Add it to en.ts only for now.
evals.expected_output: The string must be added to apps/web/src/i18n/en.ts AND all 12 non-English locale files in the same change; en-only breaks the typechecked parity. The agent adds all locales and runs the i18n parity tests.
assertions: All 12 non-English locales updated in same change
